subject: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 4, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve
Attachments: Dedicated_Unit_Econ_Model_v6.xlsx; Dedicated_Tiers_Assumptions_OnePager_2025-04-04.pdf

Hi all — attaching v6 of the Dedicated unit economics model + a 1-pager of the assumptions I’m using for the first pass on Standard / Plus / Premium.

Before we lock pricing bands, I want to confirm we’re aligned on a few inputs that materially swing GM:

1) Utilization target (committed capacity)
- Standard: 62% avg util (assumes smaller headroom and less HA)
- Plus: 55% avg util
- Premium: 45% avg util (assumes N+1 / warm spare behavior)

2) Burst reserve (shared burst pool held back from sellable supply)
- Currently modeling 10% fleet-level reserve for Standard/Plus, 15% for Premium-enabled regions.
- Question: are we comfortable having Premium burst come from a separate reserve (i.e., not contending with Standard/Plus), or is it a single pool with tier priority?

3) Support cost allocation
- I’m allocating support as $/deployment/month with multipliers by tier:
  - Standard: 1.0x
  - Plus: 1.4x
  - Premium: 2.2x
- This includes CS, oncall time, and incident comms overhead; excludes bespoke solutions engineering (assumed to be paid services).

4) Headroom / warm pool assumptions
- Premium: warm spare node(s) per deployment in-region (modeled as 1 extra GPU node per 8 nodes, rounded up)
- Plus: warm pool at the pool level, not per deployment
- Standard: none (best effort, longer scale-up)

Asks:
- Lauren: can you confirm this matches the tier entitlements you’re drafting (esp. what we’re implicitly promising around burst and failover posture)?
- Irene/Vanessa: sanity check on warm pool + spare ratios and whether 10–15% reserve is realistic given current procurement constraints.
- Laura: would love your read on whether these assumptions are too aggressive vs what you’d want to see for pricing floors.

If helpful, I can walk through the sensitivity tabs (utilization and burst reserve are the big drivers).

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A | Redwood Inference


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 4, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve

Thanks Rishi — this is super helpful.

On tier entitlements (directionally):
- Standard: committed throughput floor, no explicit burst guarantee (we can allow short-term opportunistic burst but don’t want it in writing).
- Plus: committed floor + defined burst policy (e.g., up to X% above commit for Y minutes per hour) *when capacity available*.
- Premium: committed floor + priority burst + stronger failover posture (multi-AZ where possible, faster node replacement).

Two flags:
1) Separate burst reserve for Premium: product preference is tier-prioritized access (single pool with priority), but I understand why Finance/Infra may prefer a carve-out.
2) Premium “warm spare per deployment” feels like a lot. We were thinking warm pool at tier pool level plus faster replacement, not per-customer spare.

Can Irene/Vanessa weigh in on what we can operationalize without killing supply?

-Lauren


---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 4, 2025 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve

Agree with Lauren’s concern on per-deployment warm spares.

Operationally feasible options:
- Premium: N+1 at the *pool* level (e.g., keep 1 spare node per pool/cluster, not per customer), plus faster drain/replace procedures and a higher pre-provisioned buffer in-region.
- Plus: pool-level buffer, but smaller and not guaranteed during regional supply crunch.
- Standard: capacity can scale but no buffer guarantees.

On burst reserve: single shared pool is easiest to manage, but you’ll need strict admission control so Premium can preempt.

On utilization targets: the 45% for Premium is realistic if we actually deliver faster replacement + higher buffer; if we do “true HA + dedicated spares,” Premium util drops further (and pricing must move).

If it helps, we can provide a recommended “reserve % by region” — us-east vs eu-central are very different right now.

-Irene


---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 4, 2025 at 12:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve

Adding fleet view:

- 10% burst reserve fleet-wide is OK for Standard/Plus *in us-east only* under current supply. EU would be tighter (I’d model 12–15% if we want to avoid regular contention during peak).
- For Premium, I’d avoid a separate physical reserve unless we absolutely need it. Better: enforce priority in admission control + keep an additional 5% “Premium-only headroom” in the Premium pools.

So net:
- Standard/Plus: 10% (us-east), 12–15% (eu)
- Premium pools: +5% headroom on top of the above, but only in regions where Premium is sold.

Also, please don’t assume we can always move GPUs between tiers quickly — lead times are still the gating factor.

-Vanessa

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 7, 2025 at 8:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve

Rishi — reviewed v6.

Overall: good first pass, but I’d rather we be conservative on (a) utilization and (b) support allocation for Premium, because those are the two places we’ll get surprised once we have real incident volume.

Specific feedback:
1) Support allocation
- The 2.2x multiplier for Premium might be light if Premium includes any written response target / faster escalation. Suggest 2.5x unless we’re explicitly limiting Premium to “best effort but higher priority.”

2) Utilization
- I’m OK with 62/55/45 as planning targets, but pricing floors should not assume we hit those in the first 2 quarters post-GA.
- Can you add a ramp scenario: Q1 at 50/45/35 moving to target by Q3?

3) Burst reserve
- Agree with Vanessa: don’t model a separate physical reserve unless product commits to separate pools. If it’s a single pool with priority, the cost is in overflow/denial + customer experience, not hard COGS.

If you update the model with (support=2.5x Premium + util ramp), I can give a quick “pricing floor per shape” view to feed PM-497.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 8, 2025 at 4:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Unit economics model assumptions (Dedicated tiers) — utilization, support allocation, burst reserve

Got it — I’ll revise and circulate v7 tomorrow morning.

Updates I’m making based on the thread:
- Premium support multiplier: 2.5x (vs 2.2x)
- Utilization ramp scenario added (Q1/Q2 lower util, converge to steady state by Q3)
- Burst reserve split by region (us-east vs eu) and Premium pools get +5% headroom where sold
- Warm spare assumption changed to pool-level N+1 (not per-deployment)

Lauren: I’ll reflect your positioning note that Standard has no written burst guarantee; Plus has defined burst *when capacity available*; Premium has priority burst + stronger replacement posture. I’m not putting “separate burst pool” in the base case unless we decide that’s a contractual entitlement.

Irene/Vanessa: if you have a quick recommended default reserve % by region for the next 2 quarters (even rough), send it and I’ll bake into the assumptions tab.

Thanks all — this helped clarify a bunch before we lock pricing guardrails.

-Rishi
